newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary MHB sale to go ahead despite scandal - APV.
newsitem.headline: Hungary MHB sale to go ahead despite scandal - APV.

text.p: Hungary's privatisation scandal is not likely to delay the sale of Magyar Hitel Bank (MHB) but could affect other bank privatisations, the State Privatisation Agency APV said on Tuesday.

APV Managing Director Istvan Abel was quoted by the Hungarian daily Vilaggazdasag as saying that MHB's privatisation could be completed as planned by the end of this year despite the recent dismissal of the privatisation minister and APV's board of directors.
The officials were sacked in a scandal over irregular payments of over $5 million to an adviser who negotiated asset transfers from APV to local municipalities.
APV plans to sell some 90 percent of MHB, Hungary's fifth largest bank, to one of three banks invited to bid.
According to press reports the three investors likely to bid are Creditanstalt-Bankverein and Bank Austria-Girocredit of Austria and the Netherlands' ABN-Amro Bank.
The bids have to be submitted by October 17 and APV's board of directors should select the winner within 30 days.
If the new APV board is not set up during that time, the government could itself choose the best bid and the deadline for the decision could also be prolonged by 30 days, Abel said.
APV's plan to publish the privatisation tender for Kereskedelmi es Hitelbank Bank Rt (K&H), Takarekbank and Corvinbank this year are likely to be delayed by the privatisation scandal, Abel said.
However, if APV's new board is set up within a month, at least one of the tenders could be published before the end of 1996, he said.
According to earlier press reports, all the three banks have attracted interest from foreign investors
